---
title: "Benchmarking"
subtitle: "Do the clocks separate cases from controls, across several studies at once?"
---

Score each study separately, combine the results, and run the AA1 and AA2 tests across them.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```python
res = fa.combine([r1, r2, r3], keys=["GSE1", "GSE2", "GSE3"])
b   = fa.run_benchmark(res, condition_col="condition", control="HC",
                       dataset_col="dataset")
b.summary()
```

### R

```r
res <- combine(list(r1, r2, r3), keys = c("GSE1", "GSE2", "GSE3"))
b   <- run_benchmark(res, condition_col = "condition", control = "HC",
                     dataset_col = "dataset")
b$summary
```

:::

Median absolute error against chronological age is reported but never ranked on: a perfect
chronological oracle would score best on it and be useless, because it would have no age
acceleration left to detect anything with.

→ **Why it works this way:** [Benchmarking and validation](../methods/benchmarking.qmd)
